summary.text: Roman goddess of flowering plants who, in Ovid's calendar of rites, touched Juno with a magic flower from the gardens of Olenus so that the queen conceived Mars with no father — a Roman variant of Ares' birth answering Athena's head-birth.

story.text: Ovid tells the tale in his Fasti for the Roman month of May. Juno, stung that Jupiter had brought forth Minerva from his head without a mother, sought counsel from Flora, goddess of flowering fields. Flora touched the queen with a wondrous flower from the gardens of Olenus, and Juno conceived Mars with no father at all.

The Greek genealogical spine in Hesiod and Homer makes Ares son of Zeus and Hera; Ovid's Flora preserves the fatherless Roman variant for Mars alone — a secondary tradition attested only in the Ovid lens, not in Hesiod or Apollodorus.
